Item 1 (a) (Reasons for rapid population increase): The student correctly identified and explained five distinct reasons for Uganda's rapid population increase: high fertility rate, early marriage and pregnancies, increased refugee influx, high life expectancy, and immigration effect. Each of these five points was clearly articulated with relevant explanations, earning 2 marks per point for a total of 10 marks. The student successfully provided more than the required 'at least four clear reasons'. No significant omissions or errors were identified in this section. A complete answer required at least four clear reasons for the rapid population increase, each briefly explained.

Item 1 (b) (Impacts of rapid population growth): The student correctly identified and explained six negative impacts of rapid population growth: increased crime rate, unemployment, land fragmentation and conflicts, environmental degradation, growth of slums, and easy spread of diseases.
